name: sql_validator.py
summary: Validates and sanitizes SQL queries using sqlparse to ensure safety, syntactic correctness, and policy compliance before execution.
purpose: Acts as a security and correctness gate for SQL queries—particularly those generated by AI—to prevent unsafe operations, syntax errors, and injection attacks from reaching the database.
responsibilities: Parse raw SQL strings into token streams for analysis
Validate SQL syntax and structural correctness
Detect and block forbidden or dangerous DML/DDL operations
Identify SQL injection patterns using regex and keyword analysis
Enforce query constraints such as read-only restrictions
Report validation failures, security violations, and syntax errors
inputs: Optional validation rules or policy configuration (allowlists/blocklists)
outputs: Validation result (boolean pass/fail or structured status object)
List of syntax errors, security violations, or policy breaches
Optional parsed token metadata for downstream processing
architecture_notes: Positioned within the AI backend services layer as a critical security boundary between natural-language query generation and actual database execution. Consumed primarily by ai_query_service.py to vet AI-generated SQL. Combines sqlparse token-level analysis with regex pattern matching for defense-in-depth. Follows a validator strategy pattern, allowing sequential application of independent validation rules (syntax, security, policy).
improvements: Migrate from token-level checks to full AST-based semantic analysis for deeper validation
Add support for database-dialect-specific parsing (PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, etc.)
Externalize validation policies into a configurable, runtime-updatable rule engine
Introduce query complexity and cost limits (e.g., subquery depth, JOIN count, estimated row count)
Return strongly-typed ValidationResult objects with error codes and severity levels instead of primitive booleans/strings
Add exhaustive test coverage for SQL injection edge cases and obfuscation techniques
